title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned Night Atlas. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Night Atlas
options.thesis: The family is a night sky: people are catalogued stars, kinship is the constellation you draw between them.
options.viewport: A deep navy canvas fills the screen. Portrait-stars sit on generation bands. The selected person is a brighter star with four compass add actions. A glass instrument bar floats at the edge.
options.risk: Can read as a space game if faces and names do not stay the content of every star.

raised.raise: Ghost magnitude: filtered or unfocused people stay as faint stars; the selected star is struck brighter, never the only one present.
Declination graticule: generations sit on a measured latitude grid; pan is free until a person is selected, then the view locks on them.
Name as catalog lettering: the person's name is the constellation inscription, the primary mark on the node, not a caption under a card.
Cinch, do not hide: collapsing a branch gathers that constellation into a tighter cluster; the people remain as a compressed figure.
Epoch as magnitude: birth years are catalog numbers on the atlas, readable without opening a profile.

options.label: Kinship Transit
options.thesis: Family as a transit map: people are stations, generations are lines, relationship types are route colors.
options.viewport: A dark map with colored kinship routes. The selected station grows four add stops at the compass. A compact legend names parent, child, spouse, sibling.
options.risk: This is the direction most runs in this category land on: a clean information-design tree that already looks like a product.

options.label: Concourse Kin
options.thesis: Finding family is a signed decision: yellow bands, one next step, monumental names.
options.viewport: Yellow overhead bands name the selected person and the four directions you can add. The tree hangs below as a concourse of portrait gates.
options.case: Holds audience identification: the job is finding someone and choosing the next turn. Loses product clarity: sign bands are not a living multi-generation map.
options.risk: The tree can collapse into a corridor of signs and lose who-belongs-to-whom at a glance.

options.label: Struck Gauze
options.thesis: Every relative present as a dark ghost; one name struck forward in orange.
options.viewport: A mesh plane of faint names; the selected person burns through.
options.case: Loses both axes: family historians do not identify with vacuum tubes, and a numeral stack cannot show kinship hierarchy.
options.kept: Ghost magnitude: unfocused people stay present and dim.
options.risk: Reads as an access-control instrument, not a family map.

options.label: Signal Bench
options.thesis: Kinship as a locked phosphor trace on a ten-division grid.
options.viewport: A green trace of generations over a measured grid.
options.case: Loses both axes: a family is not a waveform, and traces do not read as people.
options.kept: Declination graticule: generations measured, selection locks the view.

options.label: Name Weather
options.thesis: Names condense into the landscape the family occupies.
options.viewport: A field of letters gathering into a selected name.
options.case: Loses both axes: weather-type hides who belongs to whom.
options.kept: Name as catalog lettering: the name is the node's primary mark.
options.risk: Beautiful and unusable as a relationship graph.

options.label: Gathered Cape
options.thesis: A branch is cloth: one pull gathers a generation into a tighter volume.
options.viewport: A black field cinched around the selected person.
options.case: Loses both axes: fashion grammar does not identify as family, and cloth hides the graph.
options.kept: Cinch, do not hide: collapse gathers a cluster instead of deleting it.

options.label: Merchant Calendar
options.thesis: A painted plate above a tear-off date pad of births and deaths.
options.viewport: A portrait plate over a date grid.
options.case: Dropped from the full hand on product-truth grounds: pinup-calendar grammar is wrong for a family product that includes children. Also loses both axes as a relationship map.
options.kept: Epoch as magnitude: dates stay visible on the atlas.
options.risk: Inappropriate carrier for a family tree.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished genealogy canvas: soft person cards, clean connectors, floating product chrome. Notion plus Linear plus Ancestry, played straight.
canonCard.viewport: A cream workspace with a top-to-bottom tree of rounded portrait cards and a search bar.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every modern family-tree product by design.
